def: vast, whether in extent (figuratively, of power, mighty; of time, aged), or in number, many
kjv: [phrase] feeble, mighty, most, much, strong, valiant.

occurrences.text: How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?
With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.
Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?
He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.
Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.
Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!
Behold, the Lord hath a mighty and strong one, which as a tempest of hail and a destroying storm, as a flood of mighty waters overflowing, shall cast down to the earth with the hand.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
